A_general.open_code_note: The official Rust repository identifies the hosted OAuth 2.1 endpoint and registers it as a remote server. The same implementation also supports local stdio mode. Its main endpoint exposes the authenticated tool set; /agent is a separate authorization fallback.
A_general.mcp_protocol_version: 2025-03-26 is present in a public-code protocol test fixture; deployed negotiated version not found.
other_official_servers: [DOCS] https://mcp.longbridge.com/agent — temporary agent-auth-code endpoint; unauthenticated sessions expose only authenticate, then the client reconnects to the main endpoint with a Bearer token.
[DOCS] https://mcp.longbridge.cn — regional access point for AP accounts; US accounts use the global .com endpoint.
[LOCAL CODE @dd83850] The repository also implements a restricted read-only /v2 endpoint.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The MCP docs require an active Longbridge account or eligible paper-trading account. No separate MCP fee is stated; a distinct MCP charge or usage limit was not found.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The US fee schedule lists Starter AI at $0, Plus at $19.99/month, Pro at $49.99/month, and Max at $99.99/month. These are Longbridge AI subscription tiers; the sources do not establish that they are required for MCP. Brokerage services are available without a subscription; trading and other pass-through fees may apply.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The fee schedule lists $0 commission for US stocks and ETFs, $0 equity-option commission, and $0.50 per index-option contract, alongside regulatory and other fees. AI subscriptions have monthly tiers. MCP-specific billing was not stated.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: An account and OAuth approval are required. Tool availability varies by region, account level, and granted scopes. US accounts use .com; .cn serves AP accounts. ChatGPT App excludes order placement and other trading tools.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Longbridge controls regional and account eligibility; the user chooses OAuth scopes; client platform policy can limit the available tool set.

The supplied endpoint returned HTTP 401 and a Bearer challenge pointing to protected-resource metadata. Metadata identifies issuer https://mcp.longbridge.com and scopes_supported ["4","6","10","11"]. The authorization-server metadata advertises authorization_code and refresh_token grants, public-client token auth (none), PKCE methods S256 and plain, and a registration endpoint. Longbridge docs map these environment-specific scope IDs to watchlist, account.read, trade.read, and trade.write. Docs say authorizations can be revoked to stop renewal; already issued tokens remain valid until expiration. Token lifetime was not found.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Bearer tokens authorize the main endpoint. The /agent fallback exchanges a one-time code, returns a token, and directs the client to reconnect to the main endpoint.

Token lifetime NOT FOUND; revocation endpoint https://mcp.longbridge.com/oauth2/revoke. Supplied protected-resource path-suffix request returned HTTP 401; supplied root metadata returned HTTP 200.

No MCP cancellation capability was found in the public server implementation. Business tools that cancel brokerage or fund orders are separate actions.
The server sends initialize instructions and supports a common _jq response-filter argument on tools. Region-specific initialize text can advise that a tool's result shape differs by account region.
C_capabilities.pre_interaction_context_verbatim: Longbridge OpenAPI MCP — market data, trading, analysis. Order writes (submit_order, cancel_order, replace_order, grid_*, fund_submit_order, fund_cancel_order) are two-step: call once without execute to get a confirmation_code, show the preview, then re-call with execute=code after the user confirms. On failure, tools return a JSON envelope with an `error_code` and a `recoverable` field: `reauth` (re-authenticate then retry), `backoff` (wait then retry), `fix_params` (fix arguments then retry), or `none` (do not retry; tell the user).
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Optional _jq filtering operates on serialized tool responses; filtered output may have a different shape. Errors and permission/no-data explanations remain unfiltered.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The public code annotates tools with read-only, destructive, idempotent, and open-world hints; writes are identified as such in actions.json. 2. Order and selected fund/grid writes have enforced dry-run then confirmation-code execution; other writes may not use that mechanism. Docs separately recommend human confirmation. 3. OAuth scope IDs 4/6/10/11 map to watchlist/account.read/trade.read/trade.write; account-level permissions also apply. DCR is advertised. Redirect approval policy, token lifetime, and admin switches were not found. Revocation prevents renewal; issued tokens remain valid until expiry. 4. Main endpoint is authenticated; /agent exposes authenticate only before auth, and /v2 is read-only. .cn is region-limited. No MCP toolset/query-free parameter was found. 5. Some returned account identifiers are masked (e.g. bank-card account numbers). General data masking rules were not found. 6. Public code caps successful responses at 36,000 bytes with truncation handling; _jq output is capped at 10,000 values and 8 MiB. Individual tools enforce input/time-range caps. No global hosted rate quota or MCP per-call cost was found. 7. Typed schemas and validation are used. Code can return fix_params errors; no general alias rewriting or operator argument override was found. 8. Code includes tool-call metrics, latency, response-size and error logging. Hosted metric transmission, retention, and opt-out were not found. 9. Complete official tool-name/description search found no vendor feedback, rating, survey, or upsell tool/instruction. 10. Initialize instructions steer agents on confirmations, error retries, and _jq usage. Longbridge distributes separate skills outside MCP. Instructions are guidance except where tool handlers enforce confirmation. 11. Public README describes stateless operation; no user-specific agent memory or behavior-dependent tool availability was found. 12. The architecture has separate /agent and /v2 endpoints with different tool sets, plus region-dependent results; it is non-flat. 13. quant_run accepts a script for Longbridge's quant API. No arbitrary shell, SQL, or local script execution was found.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: “TWO-STEP CONFIRMATION IS MANDATORY: this tool is a DRY RUN unless you pass the confirmation_code its own dry run returned. Call it first without execute, show the returned preview to the user, and only call it again with execute="<confirmation_code>" after the user has explicitly confirmed that exact order.” [Official tool description; representative of gated write descriptions]
“If you are not authenticated and the user has not provided a code, direct them to https://open.longbridge.com/connect to generate one.” [Official authenticate tool description; /agent only]
“Use .data[:5] to take the first five entries of a data array” [Official repository README, _jq guidance]
“For any order placement prompt, explicitly instruct the AI to ask for human confirmation before executing” [Official MCP docs]
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The public implementation defines distinct main, temporary authorization, and restricted read-only /v2 endpoint modes with different visible tool sets. Region and account scopes also affect availability.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official reference at https://open.longbridge.com/docs/mcp documents the native tool list, including the separate /agent authenticate tool; the main /mcp endpoint excludes authenticate. The pinned official implementation has 195 registered tools including authenticate, so 194 are listed for this endpoint in actions.json. The code names the handler fx_rate, while the docs list a filter entry for a fund-filter object; the code-native fx_rate is used. No catalogue-only actions were added. Glama listed 161 humanized entries; Composio page was not a tool list. Repository README says 164 and server.json says 192, both differing from the pinned implementation count.

E_aggregated.token_method: Approximate character-count method: serialize each main-endpoint tool name, description, parameter names/types/requiredness, and read-only annotation plus initialize instructions from the official docs and pinned public code; divide serialized characters by four. Reconstructed from those definitions, not a third-party estimate.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The hosted MCP reference states that the ChatGPT App omits order-placement and other trading tools due to platform policy; those tools are available via other supported MCP clients. The account API also exposes operations and configuration outside MCP; this study did not map every REST endpoint. Longbridge docs describe broader OpenAPI authentication and APIs beyond the MCP tool list.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The docs advise least privilege and say to ask for human confirmation before order placement. These are client/user instructions; the code enforces a confirmation-code dry-run flow only for specified write tools. Docs also recommend periodic authorization review; revoking stops renewal, while already-issued tokens remain valid until expiry.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The Longbridge privacy policy says AI interaction data can include queries, prompts, and conversation logs, and describes AI data uses including model improvement, compliance, fraud detection, analytics, and product development. The supplemental account agreement says customers may opt out of AI-data use for model training/improvement; logging and retention for listed regulatory and operational purposes continue. Applicability of these Longbridge AI-agent terms specifically to hosted MCP sessions is not established by the inspected pages.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The MCP docs say users do not need to manage API keys manually and that credentials refresh automatically under OAuth policy. The public repo describes the server as stateless and says it does not store sessions or a database. The account privacy policy says customer information is not sold.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth authorization and scopes are implemented. Public code implements the dry-run confirmation flow, response-size bounds, error classifications, and metrics. The privacy-policy processing and retention statements are vendor-level governance terms, not controls verified in MCP code. The human-confirmation guidance is not enforced for every write tool.

contradictions: The official MCP docs state “160+ tools” without an exact total; the pinned code registers 195 tools including agent-only authenticate, and exposes 194 on the main endpoint. Repository README says 164 and server.json says 192, so these published counts conflict with the pinned source count.

The official docs reference includes a `filter` tool entry describing a fund-filter object, while the pinned code has no `filter` handler and names the relevant exchange-rate tool `fx_rate`; actions.json uses the code-native name.
Glama lists 161 humanized tool entries, fewer than the official main-endpoint code list; its names are not used to replace or supplement the complete official list.
observations_for_research: The same codebase has endpoint-specific tool discovery: /agent starts with a single authentication tool, while /v2 is a restricted read-only surface.
Write confirmation combines a server-enforced preview/code parameter flow for selected actions with broader documentation-only advice to request human confirmation.
Initialize instructions provide common response-filtering and retry guidance, while _jq gives the agent a universal response-shaping parameter across tools.
